newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish central bank calls for tight fiscal reins.
newsitem.headline: Danish central bank calls for tight fiscal reins.

text.p: Denmark's central bank, the National Bank, on Thursday called in its 1996 annual report for the government to maintain fiscal stringency in 1998 in order to keep the current account in surplus.

"In light of the presumption that 1997 will be the fourth consecutive year with good economic growth and that the public sector budget is expected to balance in 1997, there is a need for a tightening of public finances in 1998," it said.
"The need for a tight fiscal policy is underlined by the need to keep the balance of payments in surplus," it added.
"To preserve a surplus on the balance of payments, domestic demand must not grow significantly faster than that of other countries," the report added.
"The main goal of economic policy during the coming year is to control domestic demand to ensure low rises in pay and prices and a continued balance of payments surplus," it added.

Full-year 1996 data showed a surplus of 10.9 billion crowns, compared to 9.4 billion in 1995, but monthly figures show the balance going from a 0.2 billion surplus in October 1996 to a 6.6 billion deficit in November and a 2.3 billion shortfall in December. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
